known_limitations: The delegated qualification ran inside a transient Delegate=yes systemd unit created by the operator.  It qualifies the production code path on real cgroup v2; it is not an installed-path or production-root qualification and neither is claimed.
The trusted manager leaf holding the live controller is a disclosed residual cgroup for the controller's lifetime, reclaimed on unit teardown.  It is never reported as manually removed.

While a trusted helper is alive this controller is a child subreaper.  An orphaned descendant of this controller that no effect owns would reparent here and is not reaped, because reaping it would require waitpid(-1) and could consume an unrelated child.  The window is bounded by helper lifetime and is disclosed rather than closed.

A DeprecationWarning about fork() in a multi-threaded process is emitted when the trusted mount-namespace helper is forked.  It appeared again in the delegated qualification run.  It is pre-existing, non-failing, not introduced by this repair, and is NOT closed here.
On hosts without cgroup v2 delegation the mechanism in force remains RLIMIT and is recorded honestly.
EVID-08 remains IMPLEMENTED: CPU and RSS are OBSERVED_BEST_EFFORT and the retry counter belongs to the Milestone 3 cumulative budgets.
Milestone 3 remains forbidden and was not started.

delegated_run.detail: The operator ran the three qualification modules inside a transient Delegate=yes systemd unit under ADMISSIBLE_REQUIRE_DELEGATED_CGROUP=1, against the worktree carrying the B32, B33, B34, B35, and M36 changes.  Zero skips: under that variable a delegated test fails rather than skipping, so no result here can be a false green.

non_blocking_observations.disposition: Recorded truthfully as an existing non-blocking observation.  It appeared in the non-privileged regression as well, it is not introduced by this repair, it failed no test, and it is NOT claimed closed here.
non_blocking_observations.observation: DeprecationWarning: This process is multi-threaded, use of fork() may lead to deadlocks in the child.

platform_contract.probe_detail: cgroup-delegation=MANAGER_LEAF_CREATE_FAILED: the delegated parent /init.scope is not writable here (EACCES); a Delegate=yes transient unit is required
platform_contract.scope: This object describes the non-privileged development host on which the deterministic suite ran.  It is not the delegated qualification environment, whose properties are recorded under m2_final_protocol_lifecycle_closure.delegated_run.unit_properties.

prior_physical_qualification.scope: This transcript is historical evidence for the code as it stood at the parent commit. It does not qualify the code changed by this repair; a prior physical transcript never qualifies modified code.

supersedes_validation_report.model: Option A -- versioned historical snapshot.  The superseded bytes are preserved under a clearly historical filename and the canonical filename carries the single current report, so a third party never has to decide which of two files is authoritative.
supersedes_validation_report.reason: M2-M36.  The superseded report carried the fourth-repair terminal refusal, a limitation declaring M2-B25 implemented but not physically qualified, cgroup delegation recorded as unavailable, and real delegated qualification recorded as false -- alongside two B25 closure objects recording a 125-test delegated run that had in fact succeeded.  One current artifact therefore asserted a physical qualification and its absence.  The bytes are preserved unchanged under the historical filename and this file is the sole current report.

test_counts.note: Counts are live discovery totals on the non-privileged development host.  The skipped count is exactly the delegated physical tests plus one legacy delegated test; under ADMISSIBLE_REQUIRE_DELEGATED_CGROUP=1 those tests fail rather than skip.
